text:
The evidence can't say whether this violates forest protection rules. It shows what changed, not whether it was legal.

**What it shows:** Hansen/UMD mapped about 0.6 ha of tree-cover loss in 2022, or 3.4% of the 17.6 ha property. The JRC 2020 map agrees the area was forest, and a later year (up to 2025) was observed, so the loss is corroborated. The MGAP 2021 map classes about 0.5 ha as native forest and 0.1 ha as outside mapped forest. A further 0.2 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event.

**What it doesn't establish:** that deforestation or land-use change occurred, since tree-cover loss includes any stand replacement. It also doesn't give the cause (harvest, fire, storm or clearing), whether the change was authorized, who was responsible, or any compliance finding.

**Next step:** a compliance conclusion would need permit or authorization records and the applicable rules, plus field or higher-resolution verification of the cause.
